page: Microsoft Azure D2ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The configuration provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, translating to 4.0 GB per core, and includes a 118 GB local disk with Premium Storage capability. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance type.

Benchmark data indicates a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% for both stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests. However, due to the low core count, multi-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck; small-block read-only memory bandwidth is poor, placing in the bottom 10%, and large-block read-only bandwidth is weak, though large-block write bandwidth achieves an average rating.

This hardware profile is suited for lightweight workloads that benefit from high single-core clock speeds but do not require massive parallel processing or high memory throughput. Examples include basic web serving, single-threaded text processing, and lightweight development tasks. It is less suitable for database operations, which scored in the bottom 10% on Passmark database benchmarks, or intensive multi-threaded applications. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a low-entry hardware profile with dedicated CPU resources and local storage, making it a viable option for utility computing where high memory bandwidth is not critical.

Under benchmark testing, the server demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 25%.
